observed_code.behavior: On failed automatic zero, checks automatic_abort_allowed and then asynchronously sends the same TelemetryCommand::Abort used for manual abort.
Checks automatic_abort_allowed and then directly logs/flushed an abort packet through Router.
The Abort consumer does not retain origin/generation; it logs the received command as manual Abort.

candidate_interleaving: Automatic producer checks the pre-Fire stage and decides to abort.
Launch commits durable Fire before the producer's enqueue/dispatch or while a previously enqueued automatic abort waits.
The automatic abort can reach the ordinary Abort consumer or router after commit without provenance distinguishing it from a manual operator request.
prior_audit.evidence_limit: This is source-level reasoning about possible concurrency. No test has forced this interleaving and no captured radio/firmware failure has been attributed to it. Do not report it as reproduced or fixed.
targeted_follow_up: Add a deterministic barrier around the automatic producer's decision/enqueue and commit Fire between them; separately test an already queued automatic abort.
Exercise the actual safety and automatic-zero producers after commit, with no new abort or valve correction; preserve manual Abort as a separate authorized operator action.
If reproduced, coordinate an internal origin/generation plus a shared commit/dispatch fence instead of blanket-disabling manual Abort or weakening board watchdog/recovery behavior.

queued_automatic_zero_fix.producer: auto_zero failure queues TelemetryCommand::AutomaticAbort, preserving automatic origin until consumption.
queued_automatic_zero_fix.consumer: command_at_dispatch rechecks automatic_abort_allowed before normal dispatch; stale automatic intent is discarded after Launch/Fire, while valid prelaunch automatic intent maps to Abort.
queued_automatic_zero_fix.manual: Ordinary operator TelemetryCommand::Abort passes through unchanged; automatic errors retain automatic origin in their dispatch reason/message.
queued_automatic_zero_fix.external_api: Internal AutomaticAbort is serde-skipped and cannot be submitted as a client command.
queued_automatic_zero_fix.hitl: Existing HITL automatic-abort behavior is preserved by automatic_abort_allowed; test branches explicitly require automatic intent to remain dispatchable in HITL Launch.
assertions: Prelaunch automatic intent maps to Abort.
At Launch, non-HITL automatic intent is discarded; HITL still maps to Abort.
Manual Abort remains dispatchable at Launch.
Automatic-zero timeout regression now expects AutomaticAbort intent, not a falsely labeled manual command.
